Sample.evidence_source: The text provides Ns for specific subgroups and analyses (e.g., 'at age 36, 313', 'In the LPA, 335 participants', 'life satisfaction was only available at age 36 (n = 36)', 'psychological well-being (the groups sizes were 43, 188, and 48, respectively)', 'social well-being... only at age 42 (n = 200)'), but not a single N for the whole sample for each SWB component at each wave.

infoYearT1.evidence_source: In the present study, we used information gathered at ages 36 in 1995, 42 in 2001, and 50 in 2009.

yearT1.evidence_source: In the present study, we used information gathered at ages 36 in 1995, 42 in 2001, and 50 in 2009.

country.evidence_source: The present study utilized data drawn from the ongoing Finnish JYLS

Outcome_variable.evidence_source: We compared participants for whom information on life satisfaction was only available at age 36

sample_type.evidence_source: The initial JYLS sample consisted of 12 randomly selected complete second-grade classes from schools in the town of Jyväskylä in Central Finland.

ethnicity.evidence_source: Comparison of participants with non-participants at each age has shown that the participants are representative of the Finnish age cohort born in 1959 in, for example, marital status, education, and employment situation as given in Statistics Finland (Pulkkinen, 2017; Pulkkinen & Kokko, 2010).
ethnicity.warning: Ethnicity is not explicitly reported with percentages. While the sample is Finnish, the 70% rule for 'predominantly white/european' cannot be applied without explicit reporting.

lag.evidence_source: Data were gathered at ages 36 in 1995, 42 in 2001, and 50 in 2009. The intervals are 6 years (1995-2001) and 8 years (2001-2009), so there is no single typical lag.

M_SWB.evidence_source: No means for subjective well-being components are reported in this section.

SD_SWB.evidence_source: No standard deviations for subjective well-being components are reported in this section.
